clue.text: Prospect for gold in part of America

indicators.note: the word for gold is placed inside the name of the country

parts.note: Panama is a country of Central America
OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone goes prospecting for gold somewhere in the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' is not the miner's verb but a noun: a wide view, and 'for gold' is part of the wordplay, not the prospector's aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a broad view of scenery, the same as a sweeping vista.

clue.text: Something drunk in tea-set? Not normally

indicators.note: arranged not in the normal way, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what is being drunk out of an odd tea set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not normally' rearranges IN and TEASET together.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, so a drink.

clue.text: Course for golf tournament- English links

parts.note: the Open is golf's championship event
Sandwich in Kent has a famous links golf course, Royal St George's

explanation.surface: A golf event is staged on an English seaside links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' hints at golf but means a course of a meal; links are seaside golf courses, and Sandwich is a town in Kent with one.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of bread with a topping and no lid can be served as a dish or course of a meal.

clue.text: Girl embraces soldier, perhaps in Port of Spain

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the other piece within its arms

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
a soldier is one kind of ant, so 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.surface: A girl hugs a soldier, possibly in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port of Spain' is also the capital of Trinidad, but here it simply means a Spanish port.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a seaport on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Order a compass, say

indicators.note: say marks that the phrase is spoken, giving a sound match for the answer

parts.note: a compass, in the sense of scope or reach, is 'a range'

explanation.surface: Someone orders a navigation compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to speak 'a range' (a compass, in its sense of scope), which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To order things is to put them in sequence, to sort them.

clue.text: Shrewdness of a copper overcoming people

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something means placed above it

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men means people

explanation.surface: A policeman shows sharp judgement in overpowering a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal's symbol; 'overcoming' puts A CU above MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight, the ability to judge quickly and well.

clue.text: County needs able opener against one cricket side

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word able

parts.note: v is short for versus, against
the on side, or leg side, is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A county cricket team needs a capable opening batsman against a rival side.
explanation.walkthrough: Avon was an English county from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Avon was an English administrative region around Bristol and Bath.

clue.text: Nelson's employer

parts.note: a nelson is a grappling hold, so the one who uses it is a grappler, not the admiral's navy

explanation.definitionFit: A full or half nelson is a hold applied in the sport of grappling, so one who employs it competes in that sport.

clue.text: One prepared to take a fence

definitions.meaning: someone ready to accept or catch what is given
a fence is a dealer in stolen goods

explanation.surface: A horse is readied to jump a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver accepts things handed over, and in law the term names a handler of stolen goods.

clue.text: Is splitting up partnership sensible?

indicators.note: the first word gets inside the other, breaking it apart

parts.note: a partnership is a 'we', two people together

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether breaking up a couple is the prudent thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sensible means showing good judgement, being prudent.

clue.text: Saving part of policy there's no demand for?

definitions.text: Saving part of policy there's no demand for?

parts.words: Saving part of policy there's no demand for?
parts.note: an insurance discount earned when the holder makes no demand on the policy; 'no demand' reads as unpopular

explanation.definitionFit: Motor insurers cut the premium for drivers who have made no insurance demand, a reward for a clean record.

clue.text: Potter's art

parts.note: Stephen Potter, a humorous writer, coined the art of always staying a step ahead of others, not a potter at a wheel

explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter's 1952 book named this skill of gaining a petty advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Potter wrote the book describing the art of always getting the better of others.

clue.text: Family tension

definitions.meaning: a breed or line of descent

explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a lineage or variety within a species, and also stress or pressure.

clue.text: Add pound to augment modified alloy

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone tops up a mixture with a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bronze of copper and tin once used to cast cannon.

clue.text: Indicating position of game for late group

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Someone shows where game birds are, for a group arriving late.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter dog freezes pointing at hidden game; that stance is called a dead set.
explanation.definitionFit: The rigid stance of a hunting dog pointing at hidden birds is called a dead set.

clue.text: Not bound by: customs, so relieved of responsibility?

explanation.definitionFit: Duty-free goods escape import tax, and read literally the phrase means freed from obligation.

clue.text: Drain, on board, a second drink

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Drain, on board, a second drink': S (second) and CUP (drink) suggest S+CUP+PER, but nothing in the clue gives PER in that place, and the scan shows no clue text to check
annotationWithheld.clue: Drain, on board, a second drink

clue.text: Found club especially strong

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Someone has founded a particularly powerful club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is not the past of find but the verb meaning to cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbreakable or rigidly firm is called cast-iron, as in a cast-iron guarantee.

clue.text: A lucrative source in river one subjected to test

indicators.note: A and the mine are placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a mine is a source of wealth

explanation.surface: A profitable source in a river is put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting an exam is the person being tested.

clue.text: Join the character coming next

definitions.meaning: a printed mark that opens a run of following material

explanation.definitionFit: To bracket items is to link them together, and an opening bracket is a typed mark announcing what follows.

clue.text: Exciting film shows stream entering the river

indicators.note: the stream goes into the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A film shows a stream flowing into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspense movie is a gripping, exciting film.

clue.text: Transport subterranean gold

parts.note: sub-terra-nean, beneath the land: the land sits above the gold in this down entry
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Gold lies hidden underground, waiting to be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subterranean' does double duty: it supplies LAND and says the gold lies under it, so in the down light LAND stands above AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a means of transport.

clue.text: Imitate an Oriental priest

parts.note: to sham is to fake or imitate

explanation.surface: Someone impersonates an Eastern holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a spirit healer among peoples of Siberia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Traditional fare chaps finish'd off

indicators.note: the letters are off, out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some men polished off the traditional meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CHAPS and FINISHD; the apostrophe is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried battered fish with chips is the classic British takeaway meal.

clue.text: The leader of spies, perhaps? So-called fourth man

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word spies goes first
perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the head of a spy ring is the so-called fourth man.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Cambridge spy ring's hunt for a 'fourth man'; the real fourth man is the Biblical one, counting Adam and his first two sons.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is Adam's third son, so with Adam the fourth male human.

clue.text: Hired employee from agency

definitions.meaning: a hired worker, as in a farm worker

explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, and having a hand in something means being involved in bringing it about.

clue.text: Reckon I'm land-locked

indicators.note: I'm is shut inside the word for land

parts.note: an estate is a piece of land

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they are cut off from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land-locked' looks like one geography word; split it, and 'locked' is the container signal acting on the word for land.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to calculate roughly or judge.

clue.text: New tempo one introduced for musical work

indicators.note: the word one is brought into the middle of the rearranged letters
new means made afresh, so the letters of tempo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new tempo is brought in for a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the letters of tempo, and 'introduced' brings 'one' into them whole, unshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphonic poem is an orchestral piece telling a story or painting a scene.
